summary: Describes the Media Resource Control Protocol, developed jointly by Cisco, Nuance and Speechworks and published as input for further IETF work. It controls media resources such as speech synthesizers and recognizers over a network and works alongside RTSP or SIP. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A remote control for talking and listening machines. A program can tell a speech machine to speak this or listen for that.

questions: how do you control a speech recognizer remotely
subtitle: Remote control for media resources like speech synthesizers and recognizers.

tldr.problem: Applications that need to use speech synthesis, speech recognition, or other media processing services need a way to control those services over a network.
tldr.mechanism: MRCP defines a text-based protocol with requests, responses, and asynchronous events for controlling media resources. It works alongside RTSP or SIP for session management and RTP for media delivery.
tldr.outcome: This protocol enables distributed interactive voice response platforms where media processing happens on central servers rather than locally. It was published as an RFC to inform future standardization work in this area.

facts.label: Encryption
facts.value: TLS for control, SRTP for media

today: RFC 4463 is an Informational RFC and has not been updated or obsoleted. It was published as input for further IETF standardization in the media resource control space, and is referred to historically as MRCP version 1.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Media Resource Control Protocol (MRCP) lets client applications control media processing resources on a remote server. These resources might be speech synthesizers that generate spoken audio from text, speech recognizers that transcribe spoken audio, signal generators that produce tones and sounds, signal detectors that analyze audio, or fax processors.

MRCP does not manage the session itself or deliver the media. Instead, it relies on protocols like RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) or SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) to establish and manage the control connection, and on RTP (Real Time Protocol) to carry the actual audio or other media. MRCP's job is solely to command and control the media resources.
sections.eli5: MRCP is the command language between your application and media machines on the internet, like a text-to-speech engine or speech recognition service. It tells them what to do but relies on other protocols to set up the call and send the audio.

sections.title: Architecture and Resources
sections.content:
An MRCP system has two main parts: a client that needs media processing, and a server that hosts the media resources.

The server offers three types of resources: Transmission resources like speech synthesizers that generate audio streams; reception resources like speech recognizers that process incoming audio; and dual-mode resources like fax processors that both send and receive data. Each resource on a server has its own URL address, allowing clients to reach specific resources within a session.

The client and server communicate using an RTSP session or another session protocol. The session protocol establishes the control connection and sets up the RTP ports for media streaming. All resources in the same session share a single set of RTP ports, distinguished by different source identifiers when needed.
sections.eli5: The server is a machine with special abilities: it can speak out text, listen to speech, process faxes, or generate tones. The client is your app that asks the server to do these things. They agree on how to talk via RTSP, and the server does the media work on RTP.

sections.title: Protocol Basics and Message Format
sections.content:
MRCP uses a text-based message format, similar to HTTP, with optional binary data support for things like grammars, results, and speech markup. Every MRCP message has three parts: a start line, header fields, and an optional message body.

There are three kinds of MRCP messages. Requests come from the client and include a method name, a request ID, and the protocol version. Responses come from the server and include a status code and a request state (PENDING, IN-PROGRESS, or COMPLETE). Events are asynchronous notifications from the server, sent when a request does not complete immediately.

The protocol includes many header fields: content-type and content-length for message bodies, cache-control directives for resource caching, and resource-specific headers like voice parameters and prosody settings. Each message body may carry specialized data like SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) speech text or speech recognition results in NLSML format.
sections.eli5: MRCP messages look like simple text with labels and values. One type asks the server to do something, another type is the server's answer, and a third type tells you something happened while the server was working on your request.

sections.title: Synthesizers and Recognizers
sections.content:
The RFC defines two main resource types in detail: speech synthesizers and speech recognizers.

A speech synthesizer resource receives text or speech markup and generates spoken audio. Clients use the SPEAK method to request synthesis. The synthesizer supports voice parameters (like gender and pitch) and prosody parameters (like volume and speaking rate) to control how the speech sounds. It can pause and resume, respond to barge-in (when the user interrupts), and generate SPEECH-MARKER events at marked points in the text. The SPEAK-COMPLETE event signals when synthesis finishes.

A speech recognizer resource receives audio and attempts to transcribe or match it against a grammar. Clients use the RECOGNIZE method with a grammar that defines what utterances to listen for. The recognizer can be tuned with settings like confidence thresholds, sensitivity levels, and timeouts for detecting no input or timeout conditions. It generates a START-OF-SPEECH event when the user begins speaking and a RECOGNITION-COMPLETE event with the results when done. The recognizer can also be configured to detect DTMF (telephone keypad) tones.
sections.eli5: The synthesizer is like a voice actor: tell it what to say and how to sound, and it speaks. The recognizer is like a listener: give it a list of expected words and it tells you what it heard.

sections.title: Security and Deployment
sections.content:
MRCP messages may carry sensitive information such as account numbers or passwords, so secure communication is essential when clients and servers are in untrusted networks. The RFC requires that MRCP servers support Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt the RTSP control channel and Secure Real-Time Transport Protocol (SRTP) to encrypt media streams. Servers MUST support the rtsps: URI form for secure RTSP connections.

The RFC does not specify how the session is established with the server or how media connections are managed; those responsibilities belong to RTSP or another session protocol. MRCP messages are carried in the message body of the session protocol, so the session protocol is responsible for reliable delivery and ordering.

The protocol includes mechanisms for session management, such as the ability to stop multiple pending or in-progress requests at once, and to track which requests were affected by an operation. This helps applications clean up resources and avoid duplicate events.
sections.eli5: If you are sending secret information over the internet, both the commands to the media server and the audio itself need to be encrypted. MRCP relies on other protocols to handle that encryption.
